extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, patent renewal managers, corporate IP teams and clients of IP Pragmatics managing patent annuities in South America
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for calculating, scheduling and paying patent renewal (annuity) fees in Argentina, Brazil and Chile, including required data, timing differences by jurisdiction, grace periods and restoration/surcharge consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal timing and payment structure — Argentina
rubrics_metrics.description: In Argentina, renewals are due once the patent application is granted. Renewals in Argentina start from the 2nd year of filing anniversary (noted as the 3rd renewal year in IPRIS). Accumulated fees from the 3rd year of the filing date to the year of grant must be paid upon grant. Subsequent renewal fees are due annually before the expiry of each succeeding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It can take up to 4–5 years for an Argentinian patent application to be granted, so expect to pay accumulated pre-grant years at grant. Worked example: filing 20/11/2017, granted 28/04/2022 → pay accumulated fees for years 3,4,5,6 at grant; then pay 7th renewal on 20/11/2023 and annually thereafter. If renewal fees are not paid before the filing anniversary, there is a 6-month grace period to pay outstanding fees; failure to pay within the 6-month grace period causes lapse for non-payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal timing and payment structure — Brazil
rubrics_metrics.description: In Brazil, renewals are due on the 2nd anniversary of the filing date (IPRIS labels this the 3rd renewal year). Subsequent renewal fees are due annually on the filing anniversary date. Once the application is granted, renewal fees will increase to reflect the transition to a granted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worked example: filing 20/11/2020 → first renewal due 20/11/2022, then annually. If renewals are not paid before the anniversary, there is a 6-month grace period; if fees remain unpaid within the 6-month grace period the patent will lapse due to non-payment. The application can be restored if one responds within 3 months from the Notice of dismissal and pays the restoration fees and outstanding renewal fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal timing and payment structure — Chile
rubrics_metrics.description: In Chile, renewals are due once the patent has been granted; renewals are not paid annually. Instead, a decade's worth of renewals is paid on grant, and the remainder of renewals is paid on the 10-year filing anniversary. Effectively renewals are due twice (on grant and on the 10-year filing anniversary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worked example: filing 20/11/2020, granted 28/04/2022 → pay first renewal fee on 28/04/2022 upon grant; second renewal should be paid before 20/11/2030. If renewals are not paid by the renewal deadline there is a 6-month grace period during which payment can be made with a surcharge; failure to attend to renewals within the 6-month grace period results in lapse for non-payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for missed renewals (region-wide)
rubrics_metrics.description: All three jurisdictions mention a 6-month grace period after a missed renewal/anniversary during which outstanding renewal fees can be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country-specific variations: Argentina — 6-month grace then lapse; Brazil — 6-month grace then lapse, but restoration possible by responding within 3 months from Notice of dismissal and paying restoration and outstanding fees; Chile — 6-month grace with a surcharge if paid during grace, otherwise lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required to calculate renewals — Argentina
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate renewals in Argentina IPRIS requires the application date, application number, grant number, and grant date for the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate filing and grant metadata so accumulated pre-grant years and subsequent annual renewals can be calculated. The guide explicitly lists these four data items as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required to calculate renewals — Brazil
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPRIS to calculate and pay renewals on pending Brazilian applications, the application date and application number for the case are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide specifies these two items for pending cases; for granted cases expect additional grant details to be relevant because fees increase on grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required to calculate renewals — Chile
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPRIS to calculate renewals in Chile, the application date, application number, grant number, and grant date for the patent are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data allow determination of whether/when the grant-based decade payment and the 10-year filing-anniversary payment are due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewals calculation process (IPRIS two-step)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRIS calculates renewals using a two-step method: (1) calculate the renewal date, (2) calculate the renewal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two-step process is used across the country guides to derive which fees are due and when; accurate input data (see country-specific data requirements) are necessary for correct output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-payment and restoration/surcharge procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If renewal fees are not paid within the specified deadlines (including grace periods), the patent/application will lapse due to non-payment of maintenance fees. Some jurisdictions provide avenues for restoration under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brazil: if not paid within the 6-month grace period, the patent will lapse, but the application can be restored if one responds within 3 months from the Notice of dismissal and pays the restoration fees and outstanding renewal fee. Chile: payment in the 6-month grace period incurs a surcharge; failure to pay leads to lapse. Argentina: failure to pay within the 6-month grace period results in lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase filing status — Argentina
rubrics_metrics.description: Argentina is not part of the PCT convention; patents cannot be filed in Argentina through National Phase entry and must be filed directly in Argentina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects filing strategy: do not rely on PCT National Phase entry to secure protection in Argentina; file directly at INPI Argentina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee increase on grant (Brazil-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Brazil, once the patent application has been granted, the renewal fees will increase to reflect the transition from application to granted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for higher annuity payments upon grant; this is a predictable jurisdictional fee-structure change that should be built into renewal planning.
